cis_text.title: Use DNS Filtering Services

ai_guidance.llm: DNS filtering must block unapproved AI services and known malicious domains used for AI credential theft and tool poisoning.
ai_guidance.agent: Ensure DNS filtering is in place anywhere agents run to block agent runtimes from resolving known malicious or unapproved domains. This prevents agents from inadvertently connecting to malware distribution sites, phishing domains, or unapproved external services during autonomous web browsing.
ai_guidance.mcp: Ensure all DNS queries generated by MCP tools are routed through an approved DNS filtering service. Tools fetching web content or resolving URIs should be subject to DNS-based protection against malicious domains. Where third-party servers are permitted, use DNS policy to restrict access to approved endpoints and alert on resolution attempts for unknown domains.

evidence.rationale: DNS and other domain-based destinations may be used as alternative exfiltration channels. DNS filtering only impedes implementations that depend on resolving a known malicious domain.

technique.name: Exfiltration Over Symmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol

evidence.rationale: DNS filtering can block resolution of a known malicious exfiltration destination regardless of whether the transmitted data is encrypted.

technique.name: Exfiltration Over Asymmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol

evidence.rationale: Blocking a known malicious destination domain may interrupt an asymmetric encrypted exfiltration channel.

DNS can carry encoded exfiltrated data over an unencrypted non-command-and-control protocol. Blocking resolution of an adversary-controlled domain can interrupt DNS-based exfiltration, although newly registered or uncategorized domains may initially be allowed.
DNS filtering directly affects DNS and can also prevent connections to malicious domains used for web-based application-layer command and control.
DNS filtering can prevent HTTP, HTTPS, and WebSocket command-and-control connections when the destination domain has been classified as malicious.
DNS filtering can prevent resolution of known malicious domains used for DNS-based command and control and can sinkhole requests before an endpoint reaches adversary infrastructure.

DNS filtering can prevent a compromised endpoint from resolving known malicious domains used to host tools or secondary payloads. Transfers over direct IP addresses, approved cloud services, compromised legitimate domains, or uncategorized domains may still succeed.
Blocking known malicious or compromised domains prevents browsers from reaching websites used to exploit users or deliver malicious content.
Even when a user clicks a malicious link, DNS filtering can prevent successful navigation when the destination domain is known to be malicious.
DNS filtering materially mitigates phishing that directs users to malicious domains. It does not mitigate phishing attachments, voice phishing, or messages that do not require visiting a domain.

DNS filtering can block the destination of a malicious link delivered through email before the user reaches a credential-harvesting page, exploit site, or malware download. Newly registered, compromised, or uncategorized domains may initially evade filtering.
DNS sinkholing and reputation-based filtering can prevent resolution of identified dynamic-DNS and generated domains used to reestablish command and control.
DNS filtering services may block or sinkhole known and predicted algorithmically generated domains, for example those that have high entropy in the name.

DNS filtering can block tunnels that depend on resolving known malicious domains, including some DNS and web-based tunnels. Tunnels using direct IP addresses, trusted domains, or infrastructure not yet classified as malicious may still succeed.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.
